assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of political-economy research linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal policy to economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are leading and complementary contributors to the theoretical and empirical development of this research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped several decades of research and provides a durable framework for studying institutional sources of development and public capacity.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several connected literatures, making a sharply bounded prize citation and exhaustive credit allocation difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their analysis made political incentives and organized interests central to the modern economic understanding of trade policy.
assessment.attribution: Helpman and Grossman jointly supplied the core models and are unusually clearly associated with the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established, extensively used, and remains central to research on globalization and protection.
uncertainties: Its empirical implications depend on institutional settings and may not explain all observed trade-policy variation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods substantially expanded credible empirical analysis where persistence and unobserved heterogeneity are central.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond have distinct but tightly connected claims to the canonical methods.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been tested, widely adopted and incorporated into applied econometric practice over many years.
uncertainties: Applied use can be fragile under weak instruments, specification choices and excessive instrument counts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The use of population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and made place-based opportunity an important policy-relevant research agenda.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked empirical program; the contribution is broader than any single study.
assessment.maturity: The data-driven approach has generated extensive replication, follow-on work and public-policy influence.
uncertainties: Interpretations of geographic associations as causal policy effects require care.
Credit is diffuse across a broad collaborative research network.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on resource misallocation supplied an influential quantitative account of productivity differences and income gaps across countries.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are prominent architects of the relevant measurement and quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been deeply integrated into growth and development research and has generated a large empirical literature.
uncertainties: Measured wedges need not map uniquely to distortions, so welfare and policy conclusions can be model dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work gave economic rigor to the treatment of exhaustible resources, biodiversity and sustainability across generations.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are closely associated with foundational analyses of natural capital and intertemporal environmental constraints.
assessment.maturity: The intellectual contribution is longstanding and increasingly consequential for public accounting and environmental policy.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and inclusive wealth entails contested measurement and ethical choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research changed understanding of how trade and technological change affect local labour markets, tasks and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are central contributors to the empirical designs and the resulting labor-market evidence.
assessment.maturity: The findings have endured intense scholarly scrutiny and have reshaped debates over globalization and adjustment policy.
uncertainties: Separating trade, technology and broader local adjustment mechanisms remains empirically demanding.
The appropriate credit boundary includes related work by many researchers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion altered economic models of incentives, contracting and cooperation.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Schmidt and Falk made major complementary experimental and theoretical contributions to the social-preferences literature.
assessment.maturity: The work has had durable influence across behavioral, labor and organizational economics.
uncertainties: Experimental measures and the external applicability of social preferences vary across contexts.
The field has several additional contributors with substantial claims to recognition.
